This suit is filed by the plaintiffs to declare that their deceased father Venkataramanappa son of late Doddavenkatappa is the absolute owner of the suit schedule property measuring 24 guntas in Sy.No.14/3 of Divitige Ramanahalli village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and also for an order of permanent prohibitory injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the possession of the plaintiffs' over the suit schedule property.
2. The case of the plaintiffs in brief is as hereunder:-
Venkatalakshmamma vs Subramanya K C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40776410/
3
The suit schedule property is the ancestral and joint family property of their father Venkataramanappa, having acquired the same from the Government during the year 1961-62.
After the death of Venkataramanappa, the plaintiffs became joint owners and they are in peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property.

But, out of coercion or by misrepresentation, the father of the defendants 1 to 4 colluded with revenue authorities, managed to get the revenue records in his name without any registered document, which is evidenced from encumbrance certificate.
Their father had never and ever executed any registered document in the name of the father of the defendants No.1 to 4 at any point of time.
The defendants colluded together and tried to disturb the possession of the plaintiffs on 01.02.2021 and 01.03.2021 and therefore filed this suit.

3. After the registration of the suit and issuance of summons to the defendants, it was brought to the notice of the Court that the defendant No.1 K.C.Subramanya died on 03.08.2019 and 3rd defendant K.C.Thyagaraju died on 20.12.2012.
Subsequently, their LRs were brought on record.
The defendants No.2 to 4 filed a written statement and along with the LRs of defendant No.1 and 3.
After the amendment, the defendant No.4 has filed the additional written statement.
The defendant No.5 was later impleaded which is stated to be in possession of the suit schedule property on the basis of the lease agreement executed by defendants No.1 to 4.
It has remained exparte.
4. In the written statement filed by defendants No.1 to 4, the defendants have denied the right, title and interest over the suit schedule property to the plaintiffs.

It is contended by the defendants that the father of the plaintiffs Venkataramanappa executed a registered sale deed dated 09.05.1962 in favour of the father of defendants No.1 to 4 Sri. K.L.Chandrashekhara for his domestic and legal necessities, for providing education to the plaintiffs, for performance of the rituals of his elders and also to discharge the loan for a total sale consideration of 11,550/-.

It is contended by the defendants No.1 to 4 that the suit schedule property was the absolute property of the plaintiffs'
father Venkataramanappa and therefore, the plaintiffs sought the relief to declare that Venkataramanappa was the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.

It is also stated that at the time of execution of the sale deed in the year 1962 itself, the father of plaintiffs delivered the possession to the father of defendants No.1 to 4 and even until his death in the year 2017, he has not questioned the said sale deed.
It is further stated that this suit is filed after more than 58 years and therefore, the suit is totally barred by limitation.

5. The defendants No.1 to 4 have also contended that after the purchase of the suit schedule property, the father of the defendants No.1 to 4 converted it into agricultural purpose on 01.12.1963 and later their father gifted it to them through the separate gift deeds dated 21.03.1966, 21.03.1966,
29.03.1966, and dated 29.03.1967.

It is also pleaded the defendants No.1 to 4 were carrying out the poultry business in the portion of the suit schedule property by availing loan from State Bank of Mysore by depositing the deeds as collateral security to the bank.
In the year 1971, National Highway Authority was intended to acquire the land and the defendants No.1 to 4 have filed objections.
Later the suit schedule property fallen within the jurisdiction of BBMP and the khatha was also registered in the name of the defendants on payment of sum of 6,58,000/-.

It is also stated the defendants have leased a portion of property to the 5 th defendant for carrying out its Venkatalakshmamma vs Subramanya K C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40776410/
4 business and the 5th defendant has put up construction over it by obtaining sanction plan and the 5 th defendant is carrying out commercial activities from the year 2017-18.
The defendants have termed the suit as speculative and liable to be dismissed with exemplary costs.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings this Court has framed the following issues:-
1) Whether the plaintiffs prove that their father late Venkataramanappa was the absolute owner of the suit schedule properties even after 09.05.1962?
2) Whether plaintiffs prove their possession over the suit schedule property?

3) Whether the defendants No.1 to 4 prove that Venkataramanappa had executed the sale deed dated 09.05.1962 in favour of their father Sri K. Chandrashekaraiah in respect of the suit schedule property?
4) Whether the plaintiffs prove interference of the defendants over the suit schedule property?

5) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled for the reliefs sought in the suit?
6) What order or decree?
7. In support of the case of the plaintiffs, 7 th plaintiff is examined as PW1 and produced Ex.P1 to 40 documents.
She is subjected to cross-examination on behalf of the defendants No.1 to 4 and the defendant No.4 is examined as DW1 and produced Ex.D1 to 44 documents.

Inspite of giving sufficient opportunity to the plaintiffs to cross-examine DW1, they have not chosen to cross-examine DW1.
8. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for defendants.
He has also filed notes of arguments.
Inspite of sufficient opportunity given to the plaintiffs, they have remained absent and therefore the arguments of the plaintiffs could not be heard.

9. Findings of this Court on the above issues are as hereunder:-
Issue No.1 : In the negative Issue No.2 : In the negative Issue No.3 : In the affirmative Issue No.4 : In the negative Issue No.5 : In the negative Issue No.6 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issues No.1 to 4:-

The case of the plaintiffs is that the suit schedule property measuring 24 guntas in Sy.No.14/3 of Divitige Ramanahalli Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk is the ancestral and joint family property of Venkataramanappa and he has acquired the same through the Government.

They have further contended that though Venkataramanappa did not execute any registered document in favour of the father of defendants No.1 to 4, he had colluded with the Venkatalakshmamma vs Subramanya K C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40776410/
5 revenue authorities and managed to get the revenue documents in his name.
It is further contended that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit schedule property and the defendants No.1 to 4 have attempted to interfere over their property and hence filed this suit.
On these pleadings, they have sought a relief to declare that their father Venkataramanappa is the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.

11. The plaintiffs while pleading that the suit schedule property is the ancestral and joint family property of Venkataramanappa, even after the death of Venkataramanappa on 28.05.2017 as per Ex.P2 death certificate while filing this suit in the year 2021, not sought a declaration of their right over the suit schedule property.
Very strangely the relief sought by the plaintiffs is to declare that their father was the absolute owner of the suit schedule property.
Therefore, the court has also framed the issues accordingly.
In para No.4 of the plaint while pleading that the suit schedule property is ancestral and joint family property of Venkataramanappa, they have pleaded that it was granted by the Government to him.
The plaintiffs have not even pleaded that it was granted by the Government to the benefit of entire family.

But, in the meantime, it shall be noted that in the very sale deed produced by the defendants No.1 to 4 executed in favour of their father late K.L Chandrashekaraiah, the vendor had referred that it is his ancestral property.

Therefore, the court is required to record a finding both on the basis of the declaratory relief sought by the plaintiffs and also right of succession if any to the plaintiffs in respect of the suit schedule property.

12. It is the specific contention of the defendants that the father of the plaintiffs sold the suit schedule property to the father of defendants No.1 to 4 late Sri K.L. Chandrashekharaiah through a registered sale deed dated 09.05.1962 along with other properties.
In this regard, the defendants have produced those sale deeds at Ex.D5 to 7.

These sale deeds clearly show that the father of the plaintiffs sold the suit schedule property to the father of defendants No.1 to 4 late K.L.Chandrashekharaiah for a total consideration amount of 11,550/- on his behalf and on behalf of his son Rajanna aged 4 years and a daughter Venkatamma aged 2 years.

Though the plaintiffs have pleaded that their father had not executed any registered sale deed, when the defendants No.1 to 4 have produced these sale deeds, the plaintiffs have not even chosen to deny the same in the cross-examination of DW1.

This is the sale deed executed more than sixty years back and pursuant to the sale deed, all the revenue records were mutated immediately thereafter and continued in the name of the father of the defendants No.1 to 4 and later in the name of defendants No.1 to 4.
Therefore, there are absolutely no reasons to disbelieve the execution of the sale deeds.
13. The next question that is required to be considered is whether the plaintiffs have any right over the suit schedule property.

In the entire plaint, it is not the case of the plaintiffs that though their father had executed the sale deed as per Ex.D5 to 7, their share could not have been alienated by their father as they have a birth-right over the suit schedule property.
On the other hand, in the entire plaint, except stating that they are in possession of the property, they have not asserted any right of inheritance or succession over the suit schedule property.

Further, though the sale deed shows that it was executed on his behalf and on behalf of his two minor children aged 4 years and 2 years respectively by name Rajanna and Venkatamma, in the plaint, the first plaintiff Venkatalakshmamma and second plaintiff Rajanna have shown their age as 57 years and 54 years respectively.
This is the suit filed in the year 2021.

Therefore, if the plaint averments is considered to Venkatalakshmamma vs Subramanya K C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40776410/
6 determine the age of the plaintiffs No.1 & 2, they must have born in the year 1964 and 1967 respectively.
Hence, even according to the age given by plaintiffs No.1 & 2, they were not born as on 09.05.1962.
It is also relevant to note that it is not the case of the plaintiffs that the name Rajanna and Venkatamma referred to in Ex.D5 sale deed are with reference to them.
Therefore, it is not clear whether the Rajanna and Venkatamma referred to in Ex.D5 sale deed are the plaintiffs or not.

If the age given by the plaintiffs No.1 & 2 in the cause title are taken into account, they were not born as on 09.05.1962 and therefore the reference made in Ex.D.5 cannot be considered that it is with reference to plaintiffs No.1 & 2.
14.
In addition to this, in the cross-examination of PW1, she has categorically admitted that all the plaintiffs were born after the year 1962.
She has also stated that she was born in the year 1978 and second plaintiff is approximately 10 years elder to her.
Even if her evidence is taken into consideration, none of the plaintiffs were born at the time of execution of the sale deed dated 09.05 1962.

Therefore, even if the suit schedule property is considered as ancestral property of their father,
since the sale deed was executed prior to the birth of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs cannot claim right over the same.

15. The defendants have taken up a contention that the suit is totally barred by limitation as the suit is filed in the year 2021 in respect of the sale deed executed by the father of the plaintiffs on 09.05.1962.

If the suit schedule property is considered as the exclusive property of father of plaintiffs Venkataramanappa as claimed by them by seeking a declaratory relief to that effect,
question of inheritance or succession of the right over the suit schedule property does not arise.

Even if Rajanna and Venkatamma referred to in the sale deeds are considered as plaintiffs No.1 & 2,
they can seek for setting aside the father's alienation of property within 12 years when the alienee takes possession of the property as provided under Article 109 of Limitation Act 1963.
Therefore, it is necessary to examine as to when the possession was delivered by the father of the plaintiffs to defendants No.1 to 4.
The plaintiffs have produced the RTC pertaining to the suit schedule property right from the year 1969.

These RTCs produced by the plaintiffs itself shows that immediately after the execution of the sale deed dated 09.05.1962, mutation order was passed and revenue entries were changed in the name of the father of defendants No.1 to 4.
This aspect is not disputed by the plaintiffs.
In addition to this, the defendants No.1 to 4 have pleaded that immediately after the purchase, the suit schedule property was converted into non- agricultural purpose.
Though the defendants No.1 to 4 have not produced any documents to that effect, this evidence given by DW1 is not disputed by the plaintiffs.
A deed of partnership dated 03.04.1965 was also executed as per Ex.D10 by the father of the defendants No.1 to 4.
Later the suit schedule property was gifted in favour of defendants No.1 to 4 by a registered gift deeds dated 21.03.1966 and 29.03.1967 as per Ex.D10 to 14.
When Highway Authority has proposed for the acquisition of the property, the defendants have filed objection before the authorities on 25.06.1971 as per Ex.D16.
A deed of amalgamation was also executed on 19.08.2003 as per Ex.D18.
All these documents clearly reflect that the possession of the suit schedule property was delivered to the alienee on the date of the sale deed itself in the year 1962.
Apart from that, the father of the plaintiffs has not challenged the sale deed during his lifetime, though he was alive for more than 55 years after the execution of the sale deed.

PW1 has also admitted that defendants No.1 to 4 have received the compensation for the acquisition of the portion of the suit schedule property in the year 1972 when the portion of property Venkatalakshmamma vs Subramanya K C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40776410/
7 was acquired by the Government.

In this regard, the specific portion of evidence given by PW1 is extracted for ready reference:-
"Now one building is situated in the suit schedule property.
The witness has admitted the photograph of the building situated in suit schedule property.
They are marked as Ex.D.1 to D4.
It is true that the measurement of the building and surrounding is 95000 sq.fts.
It is true that the defendants are collecting the rent from the tenants of the building situated in the suit schedule property.
It is true that the building therein is constructed in the year 2016-17.
It is true that after 8 months of the completion of Ex.D.1 to D.4 building my father died.
I do not know that 15 months duration was taken for the construction of the building.
The suit schedule property is situated at the distance of half kms from our house.
It is true that my father was residing in house No.115"
"It is true that for the formation of road some portion of the suit schedule property is acquired by the government.
It is true that the defendant No.1 to 4 have received the compensation for the acquisition of portion of the suit schedule property in the year 1972.
It is true that on the basis of the above gift deeds the khatha and other documents are transferred in the name of defendants No.1 to 4.
It is true that they are Ex.P.3 to P30.
It is true that at the time of death of my father, no revenue document stood in the name of my father".

The above evidence clearly shows that the defendants No.1 to 4 have exercised their right, title,
interest and possession at least in the year 1972 by receiving the compensation while acquiring the portion of the suit schedule property to the Government.
16. In the cross-examination of PW1, she has also admitted that the father of the plaintiffs was residing very near to the suit schedule property.
They knew the entire progress and status of the property.

Therefore, it is clear that the possession of the suit schedule property was delivered to the father of the defendants No.1 to 4 on the date of the sale deed in the year 1962 itself and therefore,
even if the suit schedule property is considered as their ancestral property, the suit is barred by Article 109 of Limitation Act 1963 as the plaintiffs have failed to file this suit within 12 years when the alienee has taken possession of the property.
17. The above evidence also shows that the plaintiffs have falsely taken a contention that they are in possession of the property and the defendants have tried to interfere with their possession.

On the other hand, in the cross-examination of PW1, she has admitted Ex.D1 to 4 photographs which shows that multi- storied commercial complex building is constructed in the suit schedule property much prior to filing of the suit.
The plaintiffs have suppressed the same and filed this false suit.
When the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit schedule property, question of granting the relief of declaration or injunction does not arise.
Therefore, issues No.1, 2 & 4 are answered in the negative and issue No.3 in the affirmative.

8 18.
Issue No.5 & 6:-
In view of the answer given to issues No.1 to 4 as above, the suit is liable to be dismissed in its entirety.
Consequently, the following order is passed:-
ORDER Suit is dismissed with cost.
Draw decree accordingly.

The defendants No.2 to 4 filed a written statement and along with the LRs of defendant No.1 and 3.
After the amendment, the defendant No.4 has filed the additional written statement.
Later the suit schedule property fallen within the jurisdiction of BBMP and the khatha was also registered in the name of the defendants on payment of sum of 6,58,000/-.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. On the basis of the above pleadings this Court has framed the following issues:-
1) Whether the plaintiffs prove that their father late Venkataramanappa was the absolute owner of the suit schedule properties even after 09.05.1962?
2) Whether plaintiffs prove their possession over the suit schedule property?
3) Whether the defendants No.1 to 4 prove that Venkataramanappa had executed the sale deed dated 09.05.1962 in favour of their father Sri K. Chandrashekaraiah in respect of the suit schedule property?
4) Whether the plaintiffs prove interference of the defendants over the suit schedule property?
5) Whether the plaintiffs are entitled for the reliefs sought in the suit?
6) What order or decree?

They have further contended that though Venkataramanappa did not execute any registered document in favour of the father of defendants No.1 to 4, he had colluded with the Venkatalakshmamma vs Subramanya K C on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40776410/
5 revenue authorities and managed to get the revenue documents in his name.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Therefore, the court is required to record a finding both on the basis of the declaratory relief sought by the plaintiffs and also right of succession if any to the plaintiffs in respect of the suit schedule property.
These sale deeds clearly show that the father of the plaintiffs sold the suit schedule property to the father of defendants No.1 to 4 late K.L.Chandrashekharaiah for a total consideration amount of 11,550/- on his behalf and on behalf of his son Rajanna aged 4 years and a daughter Venkatamma aged 2 years.
In the entire plaint, it is not the case of the plaintiffs that though their father had executed the sale deed as per Ex.D5 to 7, their share could not have been alienated by their father as they have a birth-right over the suit schedule property.
On the other hand, in the entire plaint, except stating that they are in possession of the property, they have not asserted any right of inheritance or succession over the suit schedule property.
Hence, even according to the age given by plaintiffs No.1 & 2, they were not born as on 09.05.1962.
If the age given by the plaintiffs No.1 & 2 in the cause title are taken into account, they were not born as on 09.05.1962 and therefore the reference made in Ex.D.5 cannot be considered that it is with reference to plaintiffs No.1 & 2.
14.
Even if her evidence is taken into consideration, none of the plaintiffs were born at the time of execution of the sale deed dated 09.05 1962.
Therefore, even if the suit schedule property is considered as ancestral property of their father,
since the sale deed was executed prior to the birth of the plaintiffs, the plaintiffs cannot claim right over the same.
15. The defendants have taken up a contention that the suit is totally barred by limitation as the suit is filed in the year 2021 in respect of the sale deed executed by the father of the plaintiffs on 09.05.1962.
If the suit schedule property is considered as the exclusive property of father of plaintiffs Venkataramanappa as claimed by them by seeking a declaratory relief to that effect,
question of inheritance or succession of the right over the suit schedule property does not arise.
Even if Rajanna and Venkatamma referred to in the sale deeds are considered as plaintiffs No.1 & 2,
they can seek for setting aside the father's alienation of property within 12 years when the alienee takes possession of the property as provided under Article 109 of Limitation Act 1963.
They knew the entire progress and status of the property.
Therefore, it is clear that the possession of the suit schedule property was delivered to the father of the defendants No.1 to 4 on the date of the sale deed in the year 1962 itself and therefore,
even if the suit schedule property is considered as their ancestral property, the suit is barred by Article 109 of Limitation Act 1963 as the plaintiffs have failed to file this suit within 12 years when the alienee has taken possession of the property.
When the plaintiffs are not in possession of the suit schedule property, question of granting the relief of declaration or injunction does not arise.
